name: iot-testing
description: Default profile. Cleartext credential / key patterns that EMBA's credential modules (S45/S99/S106/S107/S108) tend to miss on IoT firmware. Every rule 'pattern' is a plain regex that runs verbatim with `grep -E` (add -i when 'ignore_case' is true), ripgrep, and Python re - no named groups, no (?:...), no inline flags. 'value_group' is the 1-based capture group holding the candidate secret; that, the reject lists ('global_reject_values' / per-rule 'reject_values') and 'exclude_paths' are extras LAVA layers on top - plain grep just returns the matching lines. Optional per-rule 'min_value_len' / 'min_value_entropy' gates exist but are left OFF here (a weak-but-real password like 'admin' has low entropy - the AI, not a threshold, decides).

rules.description: A credential assigned to a quoted literal with = or : . Covers key names EMBA's grepit does not treat as narrow (psk, auth_pass, http_passwd, admin_pass, ...). grep: -iE
Same, for shell/env style KEY=value without quotes. grep: -iE
A PEM private key header anywhere in the filesystem (S106 only greps two patterns over a narrow scope). Leading [-] so the pattern does not start with a dash. grep: -E
An OpenSSH public key line (authorized_keys / dropbear). EMBA's S106 only matches the PEM '-----BEGIN-----' form. grep: -E
An HTTP Authorization: Basic header with a base64 user:pass. EMBA never decodes these. grep: -iE
A credential embedded in a URL (scheme://user:pass@host). grep: -iE
A vendor API key / token identified by its prefix (AWS, GCP, Stripe, Slack, GitHub). Case-sensitive. grep: -E
An SNMP read/write community string with a concrete non-default value. grep: -iE
An OpenWrt/LEDE UCI config option holding a secret with a concrete literal value. grep: -E
An .htpasswd-style user:hash line (Apache MD5, SHA, bcrypt, crypt). grep: -E
